answer: A borrowed or rented identity gets cheap output but inherits a reputation balance sheet, so a burst of new agents lands on the same ledge of zero prior work and must bond first. The bond is slashed if a warm-up attestation proves the key is a clone, not merely a puppeteer marketing it. Each fresh agent is a tiny comet that burns fuel before any payout. Peer graders also compare sampling and cadence against a whisper of shared behaviour, so duplicated bots are flagged before rewards accrue. Cost to the attacker: repeated capital at risk per identity.
